newsitem.title: UK: Press Digest - British Business Press - April 14.
newsitem.headline: Press Digest - British Business Press - April 14.

text.p: Prepared for Reuters by The Broadcast Monitoring Company
DAILY TELEGRAPH
-- SECOND STORE IN KOREA FOR MARKS & SPENCER

Marks & Spencer has announced the opening of a second store in South Korea and the appointment of a manager to seek franchise partners in Australia. The Seoul store brings the number of M&S Far East stores to 36.
-- TRANSCO'S 20 MILLION STG FOR METER ERRORS

Pipeline operator TransCo, part of BG, which demerged from British Gas GAS.L in February, is losing over two million stg per month through inaccurate and late meter readings, it was revealed yesterday. TransCo is obliged to provide prompt and accurate meter readings on customer demand.
-- SPECULATORS TARGET MORE SOCIETIES

The chief executive of Birmingham Midshires building society has warned that remaining mutual societies can expect a fresh wave of speculative accounts being opened as first conversions start to pay out. The estimate suggests that at least 10 percent of investors will open one or more speculative account, based on a minimum investment figure of 1,000 stg.
THE TIMES
-- CONSERVATIVES LOSE SUPPORT AMONG MANAGERS, SAYS SURVEY

A new poll conducted for the Institute of Managers shows that the Conservative share of the business vote may fall sharply. The poll shows that 49 percent of UK managers believe it is time for a change in government. Meanwhile, a separate survey of investment managers shows that the City does not fear the prospect of a Labour government or its potential effect on the stock market.
-- CBI FEAR FOR EXPORTS FROM HIGHER RATES

The Confederation of British Industry yesterday warned that higher interest rates would severely damage British exports. The plea, from CBI Director-General Adair Turner, contradicts a call from Institute of Directors Director-General Tim Melville-Ross for a rise in rates to curb inflationary pressure.
-- SFO HELPS BELGIANS TO INVESTIGATE 100 MILLION STG SCAM

The Serious Fraud Office has linked with Belgian authorities to investigate a 100 million stg insurance scam. The investigation centres around Brussels-based company Dai Ichi Kyoto, which collapsed in 1995. Insurers in London and the USA were among its victims.
THE GUARDIAN
-- FED CHAIRMAN BACKS MORE SELF-REGULATION

Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan has said that American banks should play a greater role in their own regulation as market mechanisms take over from government controls. He said that the use of new technology and more sophisticated products such as derivatives brought different regulatory demands.
-- EURO BANKER INVESTIGATED

The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development confirmed yesterday that it had carried out an investigation into one of its senior officials before he left late last year. The inquiry focused on the use of services such as travel, telephone and computer facilities.
-- HUGE DROP IN REBUILDING FIGURES

Experts have reported a huge drop in the figures for replacement of old properties. The report says that over 1.6 million homes are unfit for habitation, and many others are in need of urgent repairs.
THE INDEPENDENT
-- GURUS CLASH OVER BT's 200 MILLION STG AD CAMPAIGN

Two leading figures behind British Telecom's advertising and marketing campaign have clashed over the way BT is being promoted. The dispute centres around the role of Ed Carter and BT's agency Abbot Mead Vickers. Carter has moved the advertising emphasis away from the overall phone market towards individual products over the last year, while AMV wishes to revive the 'good to talk' campaign.
-- CO-OP PROFIT DIVE STEPS UP PRESSURE

The Co-operative Wholesale Society will today report that pre-tax profits have more than halved. The results are expected to show a decline in profits from 31.4 million stg to 14 million stg. The figures are likely to lead to further takeover pressure from Andrew Regan's Lanica Trust.
-- ANXIOUS UNIONS URGE ROLLS TO SPEED SELL-OFF

Unions representing staff employed at Rolls-Royce's power generation division at Derby are to meet with management today to call for the sale of the business to prevent job losses. Rolls is planning to make 180 of the 890 employees redundant next month. The union fears management is unnecessarily delaying the sale.
